A.explanation: Correct. $F = pA$ and $W = Fd$ give about $920 \text{ J} = 9.2 \times 10^2 \text{ J}$ after converting to SI units.

B.explanation: Too large by $100$. This results from converting only one of the $80 \text{ cm}^2$ area and $25 \text{ cm}$ distance to metres.

C.explanation: Too large by $10^4$. This results from using $80$ and $25$ in cm without converting to $\text{m}^2$ and $\text{m}$.

D.explanation: Far too large. This results from a power-of-ten error in area or pressure conversion, not from $W = pA d$ in SI units.

hints: Notice the given $80 \text{ cm}^2$ piston area and $25 \text{ cm}$ travel must both be changed to $\text{m}^2$ and $\text{m}$ before using $\text{Pa} = \text{N m}^{-2}$.
Connect pressure to force with $p = F/A$, so the gas force is $F = pA$ acting through the $25 \text{ cm}$ displacement.
Combine the steps as $W = Fd = pAd$ and check powers of ten: $10^{-4}$ for $\text{cm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$ and $10^{-2}$ for $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Convert the area and distance to SI units: $A = 80 \text{ cm}^2 = 80 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 = 8.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^2$ and $d = 25 \text{ cm} = 0.25 \text{ m}$.
Use $p = F/A$ to find the constant force of the gas on the piston: $F = pA$.
Use work done by a constant force in the direction of motion: $W = Fd$.
Substitute $F = 3680 \text{ N}$ and $d = 0.25 \text{ m}$: $W = 3680 \times 0.25 = 920 \text{ J} = 9.2 \times 10^2 \text{ J}$, with unit $\text{N m} = \text{J}$. This is option A.
